messages:
jenny: Hey team, customer Acme-Maps reporting intermittent mid-stream silence on SSE connections. They see stream data stop for ~5-30s then client reconnects and resumes, resulting in duplicated tokens and billing churn. Happening across mobile + web. They attached a pcap and server logs: s3://acme-support/pcaps/2271112222.pcap and asked for a triage. repro steps they gave: 1) open SSE to /v1/streams with SDK v1.3.2 2) send a long generation (~1200 tokens) 3) after ~45s client sees no more chunks but TCP stays open 4) client then reconnects and resumes (resume token), sometimes missing final tokens. Can someone look at observability pointers (traces, metrics) and quick repro suggestions?

matt: ack. can you paste one request_id and the exact client library + platform (ios/android/web)? also did they hit any 5xx from our edge?

jenny: request_id=acme-req-20260310-9b2f. client: web sdk 1.3.2 (chrome 111) and iOS 1.3.2. Edge responded 200 then silence — no 5xx in the timeframe. Attached trimmed server log around request_id.

alex: grabbing pcap now. quick thought: could be TLS session renegotiation/ALB idle timeout or proxy keepalive getting dropped. any chance there's an ALB/NGINX in front that has 60s idle?

leo: from runtime side: we sometimes see HTTP/2 GOAWAYs or TLS alerts that show up as mid-stream interrupts. if the client doesn't send application data for N seconds some proxies will send a TLS-level close or GOAWAY. can you confirm if connection uses HTTP/2 or plain SSE over HTTP/1.1?

jenny: customer said SSE over HTTP/1.1 (EventSource) from browser, but mobile uses our websocket fallback with the same symptoms. pcap shows a quiet period then a TCP window probe from client, then client FIN->RST after retry.

matt: can you ask the customer to run a local repro with tcpdump + curl so we can see both sides? Example command to stream and keep verbose:

```bash
curl -v -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams
```

and run `sudo tcpdump -w client.pcap port 443` while streaming. we want the exact clock window.

jenny: they ran that. pcap snippet shows TCP keepalive/zero window then a TLS alert 0x0 (close_notify) from server followed by client FIN. timestamp range: 2026-03-10T15:12:06Z -> 15:12:10Z. putting the pcap link in the ticket.

alex: I pulled the proxy logs for that window. I see an upstream proxy GC spike and the connection was proxied to instance i-0abc1234 which logged a TLS write error: 'tls: short write' right before close_notify. CPU spiked ~95% at that exact second.

leo: that aligns with runtime backpressure/GC causing the runtime to not pump the socket and the proxy to decide the connection is unhealthy. hypothesis: long-running generation + large KV cache + a GC pause leads to a TLS alert being sent then connection termination.

matt: plan of action: 1) reproduce locally with a load that forces GC (we have a script), 2) test bypassing edge proxy (direct connect to backend) to confirm proxy involvement, 3) add temporary instrumentation to log TLS alerts + http2 GOAWAY reasons, 4) ask infra to check proxy keepalive settings and any middlebox idle timers.

alex: infra will tail proxy logs + enable extra GC metrics on that instance pool for next 24h. i also increased proxy idle timeout from 60s -> 120s on the canary to see if it reduces occurrences.

jenny: I told customer our immediate ask: 1) run curl tcpdump and share pcap window (they already did), 2) try a direct-to-backend test (we gave them a canary URL), 3) enable client heartbeats (EventSource keepalive) if possible. customer agreed to try.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-4783 assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2, slack alert sent to #eng-runtime.

matt: for repro you can use this node snippet to simulate long generation and force chunking/pause:```js
const es = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } });
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('chunk', e.data);
// artificially hold main thread to simulate GC
function busy(ms){ const end = Date.now()+ms; while(Date.now()<end){} }
setTimeout(()=> busy(1200), 40000); // simulate pause at ~40s
```

leo: if we confirm GC/pause is cause, long-term fixes: increase small object pool, tune GC, or offload streaming writers to a non-blocking I/O thread. short-term: bump proxies' idle timers + recommend client-side keepalive pings.

jenny: thanks everyone — I'll keep Acme updated and paste next pcap after direct test. assigning follow-ups: matt/leo to reproduce + instrument, alex to monitor proxy GC and logs.

matt: dropping a quick checklist for triage notes: - check TLS alerts in server logs - check proxy write errors (short write) - confirm if GOAWAY present - capture server-side tcpdump at same time window - collect heap/GC metrics for runtime instance - try direct connect and client heartbeats

jenny: noted. closing the loop with the customer now. :thumbsup:
